name: Confinement nanny agencies (category guide)
summary: MOM Malaysian confinement-nanny Work Permit vs freelance pui yuet packages — agency cut, citizen vs foreign-baby levy, and how postpartum help stacks on the newborn pass clock.
body: A confinement nanny (pui yuet / yue sao) is a short postpartum engagement — typically ~26–28 days — not an MDW. MOM’s Work Permit for confinement nannies is Malaysian-nationality only; citizen vs non-citizen baby levy and employer eligibility differ from the FDW rail — read MOM key facts before you pay an agency deposit. Agencies sell replacement cover and interview pipelines; freelancers via word-of-mouth often cost less but need clear cancellation, rest days, breastfeeding philosophy, and pet rules in writing. Forum pricing clusters move with CNY/peaks and twins — treat brochure rates as perishable. Book months ahead for experienced twin nannies. Do not confuse this with a long-term helper: SIP, security bonds, and MDW insurance floors are a different MOM stack. Pair agency quotes with the Family confinement-nanny guide for pass sequencing and with FDW agencies only when you are comparing postpartum help vs hiring a full-time MDW. This is a category guide, not a ranked agency league table. Family ops note: newborn households still hit preschool sibling haze closures — confirm whether your nanny package covers daylight sibling coverage on PSI spike days.
